The method operates in a feedback loop per frame.
*   **Performance Buffer:** A circular buffer or moving average window storing recent frame times ($T_i$).
*   **LOD Map:** A mapping from predicted time budgets to discrete LOD levels (e.g., voxel spacing, transfer function complexity, or proxy geometry type).
**Predict Time:** Estimate the rendering time for the next frame, $T_{pred}$, using the collected performance statistics.
*   If $T_{pred} > T_{budget}$, select a lower LOD (simpler representation) to reduce future render time.
*   If $T_{pred} \le T_{budget}$, select a higher LOD (more detailed representation) to improve visual quality, provided it does not exceed the budget significantly.
*   **Desired Frame Rate ($R_{target}$):** The target frames per second.
*   **Prediction Smoothing Factor ($\alpha$):** Controls the responsiveness to sudden changes.
The rendering time varies with the selected LOD.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for performance history and LOD maps.
